@pranshupant I tried to replicate the issue on colab, please find the gist [here](https://colab.research.google.com/gist/sushreebarsa/ea6485c2b210c3802c4742a97ca3d718/56498.ipynb) and confirm the same?
Thank you!
@sushreebarsa Thanks for the reply. Yes, the replication code looks good and correctly captures the issue
Are there any updates on this issue?

As per the document, for the arg dilation it states.
`An optional list of ints. Defaults to [1, 1, 1, 1]. 1-D tensor of length 4. The dilation factor for each dimension of input. If set to k > 1, there will be k-1 skipped cells between each filter element on that dimension. The dimension order is determined by the value of data_format, see above for details. Dilations in the batch and depth dimensions must be 1.`

What are the expected outcome in your case?

The documentation correctly captures what dilation does in the case of depthwise 2d convolutions. I am also following the convention mentioned in the documentation about keeping the batch and depth dimensions as 1. This is evident in the code sample that I have attached.

Basically, having a dilation value (k) > (1 or [1, 1, 1, 1]) for eg. [1 5 5 1] should reduce the dimensions of the output from the depthwiseConv2d operator. However, as can be seen in the code attached, changing the value of dilation has no effect on the output dimensions. The output tensor shape should be smaller in the case of dilation > 1.

This can also be seen mathematically in the convolution output formula here: https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Conv2d.html?highlight=conv2d#:~:text=0%5D%E2%88%92-,dilation%5B0%5D,-%C3%97(kernel_size
Are there any updates on this issue?

@pranshupant it looks like you are correct, the raw op currently ignores dilation.  For atrous depthwise convolution via [`tf.nn.depthwise_conv2d`](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/nn/depthwise_conv2d), we currently rely on [`tf.nn.with_space_to_batch`](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/nn/with_space_to_batch).

You should be using the public API endpoint `tf.nn.depthwise_conv2d` anyways, which does work with dilations.  For the raw-op, we're unlikely to add support in the near term (but instead will likely throw an error saying dilations are unsupported).
Thanks! The unsupported error message will be helpful as the silent wrong answer was challenging to debug.
Are you satisfied with the resolution of your issue? Yes No
